metadata.description: The history, family tree, coats of arms and places of the House of Croÿ, told for the family.

footer.invitationBody: This site is built with you. Suggest a photo, a story, a correction: an administrator reviews it before it is published.
footer.credits: Each image is credited beneath it.

arms.croy: Arms of Croÿ: argent, three bars gules
arms.croyRenty: Arms of Croÿ-Renty: quarterly, 1 and 4 Croÿ, 2 and 3 argent, three doloires gules, the two in chief addorsed
arms.hongrieAncienne: Ancient arms of Hungary: barry of eight gules and argent

glossary.fasce: A horizontal band running across the shield from one edge to the other.
glossary.ecartele: A shield divided into four quarters, to bring together the arms of several families.
glossary.doloire: A broad axe head without a handle, originally a cooper’s tool.
glossary.gueules: Red, in the language of heraldry.
glossary.argent: White, in the language of heraldry.

style.title: Design system
style.intro: The colours, typefaces, motion and components of the site, gathered on one page to check them in light and dark, on phone and on computer.
style.colorsIntro: Two colours, those of the coat of arms: white and red. Everything else is ink and grey. The contrast ratio is measured against the page background.
style.typeIntro: Titles in Bodoni Moda, text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. The ÿ must be perfectly drawn.
style.typeSample: A family, its faces, its stories
style.typeBody: Body text: 16 pixels on phones, 18 on computers. Short sentences in the narrative present, written for a cousin rather than a historian.
style.spacingIntro: White space breathes: wide margins, few elements per screen. Corners stay sharp, like the bands and the shield. Motion lasts 200 to 600 milliseconds.
style.motifIntro: The three bars become a separator, a loading indicator and the page transition; the two dots of the ÿ serve as bullet and marker.
style.cardExcerpt: Example text. The beginning of the story will show here, three lines at most, to make you want to read on.
style.fieldDateError: Enter at least the year, for example 1890.
style.fieldAnonymousHint: The administrator will know who wrote it.
style.panelIntro: On computers it slides in from the right; on phones it rises from the bottom of the screen.
style.panelBody: A person’s profile will open here from the tree: portrait, dates, marriages, parents and children, related stories.
style.armsIntro: Drawn for the site as crisp SVG. The family can replace them with its own files.
style.glossary: Every technical term is explained in one click: three <fasce>bars</fasce> <gueules>gules</gueules> on an <argent>argent</argent> field, a <ecartele>quartered</ecartele> shield, <doloire>doloires</doloire>.
style.emptyIntro: A section without content invites people to contribute: never a hole, never filler text.
style.menuFooterIntro: The menu is at the top of this page; the footer at the bottom. Below 1360 pixels wide, the menu opens full screen.

auth.title: Sign in
auth.intro: Family members receive a link by email to sign in. There is no password to remember.
auth.emailHint: The one you gave to the family.
auth.noPassword: The link is valid for 20 minutes and works only once.
auth.invalidEmail: This address looks incomplete. Check it, for example name@example.com.
auth.sendError: The link could not be sent. Please try again in a moment.
auth.sentBody: If {email} has access to the site, a sign-in link has just been sent to it.
auth.devMode: Development mode: no email is sent, here is the link.
auth.devUnknown: Development mode: this address has no access to the site, no link was created.
auth.confirmBody: One click to finish signing in.
auth.expiredTitle: This link is no longer valid
auth.expiredBody: It has already been used or it has expired. Ask for a new one, it arrives within seconds.

email.subject: Your sign-in link · House of Croÿ
email.line2: Here is your link to sign in to the family site. It is valid for {minutes} minutes and works only once.
email.footer: If you did not ask for anything, simply ignore this message.

demo.bannerBody: The “Exemple” family is fictional: it is there to try out the site and goes away in one click.

overview.title: Hello
overview.intro: The site comes empty: the family fills it, at its own pace. Here is where to start.
overview.assistantIntro: Five steps that bring the site to life.
overview.gedcomHint: Already have a tree in a genealogy program?

arms.title: Upload the coat of arms
arms.body: The high-resolution arms file, for the home page and the Arms page.

home.title: Write the home page summary
home.body: Three or four sentences: where the family comes from, how it rose, where it lives today.

ancestors.title: Add the first ancestors
ancestors.body: Three people are enough to see the tree take shape.

photos.title: Send the first photos
photos.body: Portraits, family pictures: they give faces to the tree.

cousins.title: Invite three cousins
cousins.body: Everyone can then suggest their memories, which you approve.

tree.title: Tree entry
tree.count: {count, plural, =0 {No one} one {# person} other {# people}}
tree.emptyBody: Yourself, a grandparent or the oldest ancestor you know: then add their parents, partner and children with a simple “+”.
tree.deleteConfirm: Delete {name} and their links? The journal keeps a record to undo it.

person.dateHint: As you know it: 1890, about 1890, 12 March 1890…
person.notUnderstood: Date not understood. Try 1890, about 1890 or 12/03/1890.
person.deceasedHint: Tick it even without a date of death: a living person stays hidden from the public.
person.publishedHint: Untick to keep the profile as a draft.

errors.name: Give at least a first name or a surname.
errors.date: Date not understood. Try 1890, about 1890 or 12/03/1890.
errors.save: Saving did not work. Please try again.

import.title: Import a tree
import.intro: A tree already entered in a genealogy program can be loaded here in one go, as a GEDCOM file. Nothing is written before you confirm.
import.fileHint: .ged file exported from Geneanet, Heredis, Ancestry, Gramps…, 4 MB at most.
import.duplicates: {count, plural, one {# person seems to be in the tree already.} other {# people seem to be in the tree already.}}

warnings.dates: {count, plural, one {# date was not understood and will be left empty:} other {# dates were not understood and will be left empty:}}
warnings.notes: {count, plural, one {# note will not be imported: it might hold private information.} other {# notes will not be imported: they might hold private information.}}
warnings.missing: {count, plural, one {# link points to a person missing from the file.} other {# links point to people missing from the file.}}

import.publishHint: Living people stay hidden from the public in any case.
import.reuseHint: Same first name, surname and year of birth: the existing profile is reused instead of duplicated.
import.doneBody: {people} people added, {unions} unions, {links} parent links; {reused} people already present were reused.

errors.size: This file is larger than 4 MB. Export the tree without media.
errors.format: This file is not in GEDCOM format.
errors.server: The import did not go through. Nothing was changed.

demo.title: Demonstration data
demo.intro: To try the site before filling it, load a fictional family: the “Exemple” family.

points.people: About twenty people over six generations, with example titles, branches, places, events and stories.
points.living: Five of them are “living”: you will see how the public only sees a “Living person”.
points.content: Everything is clearly marked as an example and a banner says so on every page.
points.removal: One click removes it all: the family’s own profiles are not touched.

demo.removeConfirm: Delete the whole “Exemple” family? The family’s real profiles will not be touched.
